Inspector

Pick a different entity on the left and watch the pane change shape, not just content. That is the whole point of this rebuild. The selection strip is the workbench driving the pane; it is not a redesign of Hierarchy, which is hierarchy.html.

Four things are gone, and the reason is the same each time

What was thereWhy it went
Subclasses 0, Descendants 0, Direct instances 0 on an individualThree facts that are structurally zero for any individual and can never be anything else. Usage now reports what the subject's kind can actually have. Select a class and those rows come back as real numbers
More properties hiding nine of twelve statementsThe statements are the content. Hiding three quarters of them behind a disclosure and then printing a count of what you hid is the same fact told twice, badly
12 statements describe this entity plus Open source editorA count where the content belongs. The table is in the pane; Details is still one click away for the source
A separate Types widget with Add and Remove at the far edgerdf:type is a predicate like any other, and the statement table already adds and removes values of a predicate. One editor, not two

Where it was failing its own policy

docs/adaptive-pane-ux.md carries a per view row for the Inspector: "Header save state, identity, grouped statements and usage / IRI withdraws; predicate column narrows to 118 px / Usage withdraws; header save state and statement table remain." InspectorPanel.tsx never wraps AdaptivePane, so none of that happens. It does here, at exactly 118 pixels.

Two published sentences this supersedes

"Inspector submits its existing form through an associated Apply button in the fixed footer."

Superseded. The save state and its actions live in the action row, which is where this view already reported saved state, so the pane carries one save line instead of two. That also makes withdrawing a region safe: if the state lived in a footer that a shallow pane removes, you would lose the fact that unapplied edits exist.

"IRI withdraws; predicate column narrows to 118 px ... secondary disclosures"

The IRI and the column width are implemented as written. The secondary disclosures are not, because they were the More properties mechanism, and your instruction that this view is awful supersedes it.

What is real here

Rename with live validation, grouped multi value predicates with the three value budget and a more expander, add and remove values, asserted against inferred, kind aware usage, and a draft that is per subject: edit one entity, select another, come back, and your draft is still there with its validation intact. Reasoning is not implemented; inferred statements are marked from seeded data, and the file says so rather than pretending to a reasoner.
